## Exact unsatisfied requirement and evidence

Original 21-08.b still requires applicable median and p95 increases to remain within `max(0.25 ms, 10% of baseline)`, with meaningful owner populations, rates and worker accounting. [Focused independent cost review](evidence/r0021-terminal-20261021/reviews/events-r123-focused-cost-decision-r1.json) retains all concerning measurements and their limitations; [r123 originals](evidence/r0021-terminal-20261021/r123/README.md) remain unchanged.

The once-per-document `head.prepareNativeFirstPaint` evidence is one actual invocation per side, not a warmed statistical population:

| Scene | Baseline total | Candidate total | Added observed work |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Night | 53.350 ms | 143.161 ms | 89.811 ms |
| Twilight | 125.708 ms | 242.272 ms | 116.564 ms |
| Day | 183.765 ms | 233.216 ms | 49.451 ms |

The recorded arithmetic bounds fail. Source inspection identifies added catalogue rendering/join and initial lunar composition/encoding; the whole-head interval does not isolate a Moon-only cost. This is real additional synchronous startup work. Simply deleting those operations would remove required principal content. Earlier corrections already removed unstable callback allocation, repeated encoder initialization and the redundant deep-night UI H1 pass. No further small, causally supported reduction is established by these records; irreducibility or optimal performance is not claimed. The accepted absolute startup results remain within their independent bounds, but do not waive these increases.

Recurring `sky.accept` remains concerning but unmatched:

| Actual event window | Counts A/B | Median A/B | p95 A/B |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Twilight startup through final | 6 / 3 | 138.622 / 156.918 ms | 200.223 / 176.447 ms |
| Twilight clock-minute change | 6 / 4 | 145.936 / 130.896 ms | 183.568 / 165.933 ms |
| Day startup through final | 6 / 4 | 155.594 / 162.190 ms | 222.567 / 231.310 ms |
| Day clock-minute change | 6 / 4 | 148.450 / 160.541 ms | 199.104 / 179.261 ms |

These elapsed main-thread costs can affect responsiveness. The retained acquisition has unequal natural windows and lacks immutable per-event scene/raster joins and same-side variability; the opposite twilight directions cannot establish a causal regression estimate or a PASS. Observed natural acceptance rates of approximately 0.217–0.291/s do not show runaway cadence, but are not complete rate certification. Current-initial replacement on minute/clock discontinuity reaches approximately 82 ms at night/twilight; pooling those creations with cheap no-ops would hide their cost.

The worker records establish elapsed intervals, **not worker CPU time**. TA3 resource success also does not establish comparable positive-mask preparation/export/initiation/completion/rejection/commit cost and rates. An unchanged-weather read is not an accepted unchanged refresh; missing accepted target/DPR events receive no credit. No absent baseline function is assigned zero cost.

TA2 covers Firefox submillisecond measurement limitations and permits actual-lifetime owner evidence; it does not waive Chromium numerical increases. TA5 covers only warmed Chromium `main.paint`/`main.render` uncertainty. TA1/TA4 concern their stated presentation evidence, and TA3 changes bounded allocation permission. None approves the residual costs above.

## Recommended single decision — proposed, not effective

For this exact candidate and unchanged runtime only:

1. **Accept the disclosed one-time feature cost.** Accept the additional catalogue/initial-lunar startup work with the three recorded total costs/increases above and retained arithmetic failures. Describe this as explicitly accepted added feature work, never quantitative non-regression. Keep all applicable absolute startup, currentness, quality and resource bounds binding.
2. **Accept a narrowly named residual performance evidence exception.** Record remaining actual-event cost/rate qualification as **UNVERIFIED — OWNER-APPROVED EVIDENCE EXCEPTION**, limited to recurring twilight/day `sky.accept`, current-initial replacement and affected actual startup/weather/target/DPR events, asynchronous positive-mask publication cost/rate accounting, and worker CPU. Preserve the observed costs, unmatched populations, missing events and wall/CPU distinction. This accepts disclosed residual responsiveness/CPU risk; it does not assert that a measured regression has been disproved or that these events satisfy the original numerical allowance.
3. **Retain the boundary.** The original numerical allowance remains unchanged outside those exact candidate-specific dispositions. Every demonstrated product defect, stale publication, resource-capacity violation, scientific failure or nonexcepted timing failure still requires correction. No additional Firefox profiling, broad instrumentation rebuild or unchanged capture repeat is authorized or required by accepting this proposal.

If the owner does not accept this tradeoff, the affected predicates remain unresolved. A semantically matched native twilight job could discriminate one recurring component, but cannot discharge the known startup feature cost, missing event classes or worker CPU. The retained evidence does not justify pretending that one more unchanged campaign would qualify all of them. Additional performance qualification would need a separately specified, decision-changing scope rather than a blanket retry.

After explicit approval, the executor can record the exact amendment, have the same independent reviewer consume it against the existing matrix, freeze the resulting PR head/base/tree/runtime and present the reserved production merge decision. **This proposal does not approve merge.** Delivery, served-byte verification, independent `CLOSE-R0021`, certificate-first comment and intentional completed issue closure remain conditional on the later exact-head/base merge approval.
